transcript: Header: Date: 2026-03-11 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen, Owen Patel, Jasper Lee (Redwood) - Rajiv Menon, Laura Kim, Tom Alvarez, Sofia Reyes (Cardinal HealthTech)
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: canary plan, monitoring, runbook, final benchmarks, and security follow-ups.
[00:18] Tom: yep, thanks. we really want a low-risk cutover; minimal customer impact. the 99th pct latency and error budget are the blockers for ops.

[00:36] Owen: understood. from the POC we've seen median latencies good, the 99th needs a bit more tuning - likely batching and kv cache config. note, transcription might say 'KV cash' in auto notes but we mean KV cache.
[00:55] Rajiv: quick question - do you recommend A/B or canary? we have a hypothesis test to run for quality but also want safety.

[01:12] Maya: good question. recommend a canary-first approach: small % of real traffic, 2 week ramp, watch SLOs and quality metrics. A/B is fine if you need parallel model comparison, but canary gives simpler rollback semantics.
[01:40] Laura: for traffic split mechanics - will Redwood control routing or do we? we want the ability to route specific customer segments to the canary.

[01:58] Owen: Redwood can do policy-based routing - by header, user id hash, region. we can hand over control to your infra with feature flags; the easiest is to start with percentage-based ramp managed by Redwood console.
[02:22] Sofia: what about observability - what dashboards do we need in place before we start?

[02:35] Jasper: priority dashboards: token-level cost, 50/95/99 latency, error rate, model quality metrics (regression delta on sample prompts), CPU/GPU saturation, and KV cache hit rate. alerts on 99 latency crossing threshold or error% spikes.
[02:58] Tom: what's a reasonable threshold for 99th? our SLA target is 450ms for common prompts. in POC current 99 is around 600ms peak.
[03:16] Owen: i'd set the canary threshold at 520ms for the first week, then 480ms as we tune. also include a quality gate: if regression > 2% on the acceptance set then pause the ramp.
[03:38] Rajiv: regression tests - we'll provide a seed prompt set and acceptance criteria. Owen, you mentioned caching and quantization - any changes needed pre-cutover?

[03:56] Owen: for the cutover we recommend enabling prefix caching and a conservative batching policy; we don't want batch sizes that push tail latency. quantization profile is already set in the POC image - we may tighten kernel selection for long-context requests.
[04:20] Maya: runbook items: pre-check checklist, cutover steps, validation checks, rollback steps, post-mortem template. we'll draft and share. Jasper will attach security checklist as well.
[04:38] Jasper: security notes - we'll include KMS integration steps, where keys live, and audit log locations. also include how to confirm no customer data persisted in logs beyond retention policy.
[04:55] Laura: retention - ops wants 90 day logs for tracing, but compliance maybe 365. can we configure retention per artifact?
[05:10] Owen: yes, retention is configurable; longer retention is an add-on for hosted customers, but for Dedicated/Private it's configurable. we'll note pricing implications in the doc.
[05:28] Tom: rollback strategy - do we just flip traffic back to old endpoint? any warmup concerns?

[05:40] Maya: two-tier rollback: immediate traffic cut to fallback model variant (0-2min), then gradual fallback of infra if needed. we will keep previous model warm (KV cache will cold start though - expect a spike; include that in runbook).
[05:58] Rajiv: we need to document expected cold-start spike and mitigate via short 5-10% warm traffic before full cutover, agreed.
[06:10] Sofia: can we set automated rollback if key metrics fail?
[06:18] Owen: yes, Redwood can autopilot rollback on configured thresholds (error% or 99 latency); we'll show config in the runbook example.

[06:35] Maya: timeline proposal: share runbook by Fri (2026-03-13), run benchmarks mid next week, confirm change window by 2026-03-17, kick-off canary 2026-03-22 with 2 week ramp and go/no-go on 2026-03-25.
[06:55] Laura: sounds good, but can we shift the kick-off to weekend? our ops prefers Sunday 2-4am PT. we'll confirm by Tue.
[07:12] Jasper: i'll upload the security artifact bundle today - SOC2 Type II summary, KMS integration guide, and audit log locations - link will be in the CRM record.
[07:28] Rajiv: benchmarks - please include 95 and 99 latency with production-like concurrency and sample distribution. also capture token-level cost delta.

[07:45] Owen: yes, will do. note: some of the POC transcriptions show 'redwood dedicated' as 'red wood dedicated' in auto text - minor but usual. we'll attach raw benchmark CSV and a summarized sheet.
[08:05] Tom: any legal sign-offs needed from our side? procurement already started the SOW review. we need the security addendum signed before private data flows start.
[08:18] Maya: understood, we'll surface the security addendum and the hosting options (hosted with encrypted-at-rest, dedicated, private). Jasper to circle with legal artifact links.
[08:33] Sofia: final question - during canary, can we route only certain enterprise customers?
[08:42] Owen: yes, we can route by API key, tenant id, or percentage+hash. we'll show a sample routing rule in the runbook.

[09:00] Maya: ok let's recap actions and owners. (brief recap) will share runbook, Jasper uploads security bundle, Owen runs benchmarks, Laura confirms change window, Rajiv finalizes acceptance criteria.
[09:20] Tom: thanks everyone. we'll review the runbook internally and revert with comments. appreciate the detailed plan.
[09:30] Maya: thanks all - we'll follow up via CRM and schedule the canary kick-off. meeting adjourned.

Notes: auto transcription had some small errors, speaker overlaps, and some product names slightly garbled. Links referenced: runbook draft (to be uploaded), benchmark spreadsheet (to be uploaded), security bundle link (to be uploaded).
